items.statement: Every reconciliation exception must be addressable by a stable identity of (runId, tradeId, settlementDate, reason), scoped to that single run instance, so a resolution can be unambiguously attached to it.
items.rationale: Resolves AMB-1: exceptions have no cross-run identity, so identity is scoped per-run.

items.statement: A maker must be able to propose a resolution for an exception by submitting one reason code from a fixed enumerated set (FALSE_POSITIVE, MANUAL_MATCH_CONFIRMED, PENDING_CUSTODIAN_CORRECTION, WRITE_OFF_APPROVED, DUPLICATE_DATA_ENTRY) plus a free-text evidence note of at least 1 character.
items.rationale: Core capability requested in intent.goals; the fixed set was confirmed with Compliance (AMB-5).

items.statement: A checker who is a different identity from the maker must approve or reject a proposed resolution before it is considered final; the system must reject an approval attempt where checker identity equals maker identity.
items.rationale: Maker-checker separation is a hard requirement with no exception path (AMB-2).

items.statement: Every lifecycle transition (PROPOSED, APPROVED, REJECTED) must be recorded as a new, immutable event in the audit event store; the store must provide no application-level operation that updates or deletes an existing event.
items.rationale: Append-only history is a stated goal and a compliance requirement.

items.statement: Given the ordered sequence of events for a single exception identity, the system must be able to reconstruct its current state (no resolution attempted, pending approval, approved, or rejected) purely by replaying those events in order.
items.rationale: An append-only history is only useful if current state is deterministically derivable from it; this also enables the export in REQ-8.

items.statement: If a proposal is submitted for an exception identity that already has a pending or resolved (approved/rejected) state, the system must reject the new proposal with a conflict response rather than creating a second concurrent pending state.
items.rationale: Resolves AMB-3: first accepted proposal wins; prevents duplicate/conflicting final states under concurrency.

items.statement: A resubmission of the same proposal request (identical exception identity, maker, reason code and evidence, carrying the same client-supplied idempotency key) after a client-side timeout or retry must not create a second audit event; the system must return the original result.
items.rationale: Idempotency requirement so retried network calls do not corrupt the audit trail or create duplicate pending proposals.

items.statement: Compliance must be able to export all audit events for exceptions whose most recent event falls within a given date range, in a CSV file containing exception identity, all lifecycle events with timestamps, actor identities, reason codes and evidence, ordered by exception identity then event time.
items.rationale: Stated goal; CSV format confirmed sufficient with Compliance (AMB-4).

items.statement: Every lifecycle transition must emit a telemetry event containing only the event type, exception identity, actor role (maker/checker), reason code, and timestamp — never trade amounts, counterparty identifiers, settlement account numbers, or free-text evidence content.
items.rationale: Telemetry goal combined with the no-sensitive-logs constraint from discovery.
